name: Grey aqua
lede: Grey aqua is a muted, greyed blue-green that our library carries as an English rendering of Mizu-iro, a traditional Japanese water color, close enough to Grey teal that only half a unit of greenness separates them.

sections.title: A water color, translated
sections.body:
Our color library lists Grey aqua's source as a traditional Japanese name, Mizu-iro (水色), glossed there as "aqua blue color" [1]. *Mizu* means water and *iro* means color, so the literal sense is closer to "water-color" than to the ocean-adjacent word "aqua" that this English rendering chose [1]. Book sources on Japanese traditional colors were not consulted directly here, so that gloss and translation rest on the library alone [1].

The nearest named color is [[grey-teal|Grey teal]], 4.8 units away and bluer; [[grey-teal|Glaucous Blue]] sits at the same distance, also bluer [2]. In Munsell terms Grey aqua sits near 4.7BG 6.6/2.5: a pale, low-chroma blue-green [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Grey aqua appears in 204 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed, more common than 62 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 19 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.4 times the expected rate, and is most over-represented among Impressionist works, at 4.4 times expected [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light [3]. The earliest match, in a work by Andrea del Castagno, is dated 1450, within the archive's documented range for this name, with no earlier record to compare it against here, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
